verses.text: The group of prophets said to Elisha, "Look, the place where we live and meet with you is too small for us.
Let us go to the Jordan River. Each of us can get a log there, and we can build a place to live." Elisha said, "Go."
Then one of them said, "Please come with us, your servants." Elisha answered, "I will come."
So he went with them. When they reached the Jordan, they began cutting down trees.
As one of them was cutting down a tree, the iron axe head fell into the water. He cried out, "Oh no, master! It was borrowed!"
The man of God asked, "Where did it fall?" When he showed him the place, Elisha cut a stick, threw it into the water there, and made the iron float.
He said, "Pick it up." So the man reached out his hand and took it.
The king of Syria was at war with Israel. After talking with his officers, he said, "I will set up my camp in such and such a place."
But the man of God sent word to the king of Israel: "Be careful not to pass that place, because the Syrians are going down there."
So the king of Israel sent word to the place the man of God had warned him about. Again and again Elisha warned him, and the king was on his guard there, not just once or twice.
This made the king of Syria very upset. He called his officers and demanded, "Tell me! Which one of us is on the side of the king of Israel?"
One of his officers said, "None of us, my master the king. It is Elisha, the prophet in Israel. He tells the king of Israel even the words you speak in your bedroom."
The king said, "Go and find out where he is, so I can send men to capture him." He was told, "He is in Dothan."
So he sent horses, chariots, and a large army there. They went at night and surrounded the city.
Early the next morning, the servant of the man of God got up and went outside. He saw an army with horses and chariots all around the city. "Oh no, master! What will we do?" he asked.
Elisha answered, "Do not be afraid. Those who are with us are more than those who are with them."
Then Elisha prayed, "LORD, please open his eyes so he can see." The LORD opened the young man's eyes, and he looked and saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
As the enemy came down toward him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, "Please strike these people with blindness." So the LORD struck them with blindness, as Elisha had asked.
Elisha told them, "This is not the right road, and this is not the right city. Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are looking for." And he led them to Samaria.
When they had entered Samaria, Elisha said, "LORD, open these men's eyes so they can see." The LORD opened their eyes, and they looked and saw that they were in the middle of Samaria.
When the king of Israel saw them, he asked Elisha, "My father, should I kill them? Should I kill them?"
Elisha answered, "Do not kill them. Would you kill people you had captured with your own sword and bow? Give them food and water so they can eat and drink, and then send them back to their master."

So the king prepared a great feast for them. After they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went back to their master. After that, Syrian raiding parties stopped coming into Israel's land.
Some time later, Ben-Hadad king of Syria gathered his whole army and marched up and surrounded Samaria.
There was a terrible famine in the city. The siege lasted so long that a donkey's head sold for eighty pieces of silver, and a small cup of dove's dung sold for five pieces of silver.
One day, as the king of Israel was walking along the city wall, a woman cried out to him, "Help me, my master the king!"
He answered, "If the LORD does not help you, how can I help you? Do I have grain from the threshing floor or wine from the winepress?"
Then the king asked her, "What is the matter?" She answered, "This woman said to me, 'Give up your son so we can eat him today, and tomorrow we will eat my son.'
So we cooked my son and ate him. The next day I said to her, 'Give up your son so we can eat him.' But she has hidden her son."
When the king heard what the woman said, he tore his clothes. As he walked along the wall, the people looked and saw that he was wearing sackcloth under his clothes, next to his skin.
He said, "May God punish me, and even more, if Elisha son of Shaphat still has his head on his shoulders by the end of today!"

Elisha was sitting in his house, and the leaders of the city were sitting with him. The king sent a messenger ahead. But before the messenger arrived, Elisha said to the leaders, "Do you see how this murderer is sending someone to cut off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold it shut against him. Isn't the sound of his master's footsteps right behind him?"
While Elisha was still talking with them, the messenger came down to him. The king said, "This disaster is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"
